instruction: Disable the automatic screen dimming by turning off 'Automatic screen brightness' in power settings.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling idle activation (automatic screen dimming). The config sets it to true initially, and the task is to set it to false. Evaluator verifies the setting returns 'false' (newline included).

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction contains semantic mismatch: mentions 'Automatic screen brightness' but verifies screensaver idle-activation-enabled
'Automatic screen brightness' typically refers to adaptive brightness based on ambient light (org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power ambient-enabled), not idle screen dimming
The gsetting being verified (org.gnome.desktop.screensaver idle-activation-enabled) controls idle-based screen dimming/screensaver, which is different from automatic brightness adjustment
Evaluator logic itself is technically sound: getter correctly reads the gsetting, metric correctly checks exact match with 'false\n', expected value is correct
If instruction were corrected to say 'Disable automatic screen dimming when idle' or 'Disable screensaver idle activation', the evaluator would be perfect
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix instruction text to accurately describe what's being verified: 'Disable the automatic screen dimming by turning off screensaver idle activation in power settings' or 'Disable automatic screen dimming when idle in screensaver settings'

Alternatively, if the instruction truly wants to verify automatic brightness: change gsetting to 'org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power ambient-enabled' or the correct setting for adaptive brightness on the target GNOME version
